title: Workflow manifest
description: Manifest for the direct MaaS workflow runner. Describes either a fan-out of independent task briefs to parallel isolated claude-maas delegates, or a single sub-orchestration brief handed to one bounded claude-maas invocation. There is no HTTP router, no LiteLLM, no Sidecar, and no model fallback chain: every worker connects directly to the Huawei MaaS native Anthropic Messages API using model glm-5.2.

mode.description: fanout: run each item brief in an isolated delegate worker. suborchestrate: pass the whole brief to a single bounded claude-maas -p invocation.

run_id.description: Stable identifier for this workflow run. Used as the per-run directory name under ~/.claude-hybrid/workflows/. Restricted to a safe filename charset (no path separators).

items.description: Ordered list of task briefs for fanout mode. Each item runs in its own delegate worker. Item scopes must be pairwise disjoint.

brief.description: The single task brief for suborchestrate mode.

concurrency.description: Maximum number of parallel delegate workers for fanout mode. Clamped to [1, MAX_CONCURRENCY].

max_turns.description: Bounded turn limit for suborchestrate mode (propagated to claude-maas --max-turns).

item_timeout.description: Per-item delegate timeout in seconds for fanout mode.

verification_timeout.description: Aggregate verification timeout in seconds for the whole workflow run.

cwd.description: Working directory for delegate workers and acceptance commands.

task_type.description: Category of work. image is rejected before launch by the delegate.

goal.description: Natural-language description of the task goal.

scope.description: File paths the task may read or modify. For fanout mode, scopes across items must be pairwise disjoint.

acceptance.description: Shell command whose exit code determines task success.

item_id.description: Optional stable identifier for this item. When omitted, a stable zero-padded index id (item-000, item-001, ...) is assigned. Restricted to a safe filename charset (no path separators).
